This question tests ability to design a runtime-extensible backend with a clean interface, minimal FAB (feature-flag) API, and safe runtime swapping.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Dynamic circuit-breaking with runtime rule extension is common in large-scale systems but hard to implement safely. This tests how a candidate balances performance, correctness, and distribution.

## Key Concepts
- Circuit-breaker state per endpoint
- Runtime registries and factories
- Distributed state and synchronization
- Testing concurrent trips and race conditions

## Code Example
```javascript
```javascript
interface CircuitBreakerRule {
  name: string
  shouldTrip(ctx: any): boolean
  onStateChange?(ctx: any): void
}
type RuleFactory = () => CircuitBreakerRule
class Registry {
  private map = new Map()
  register(name, factory){ this.map.set(name, factory) }
  create(name){ const f = this.map.get(name); return f ? f() : null }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you persist circuit-breaker state across a cluster?
- How would you test time-based thresholds and backoff without slowing tests?

## Why This Is Asked

Gateways must adapt routing logic without redeploys; runtime policies test flexibility and thread-safety.

## Key Concepts

- Strategy and Registry patterns
- Precedence and isolation
- Concurrency-safe dynamic registration

## Code Example

```javascript
interface Policy {
  matches(req: Request): boolean
  routeFor(req: Request): string
}
class PolicyRegistry {
  register(name: string, p: Policy, priority?: number): void
  resolve(req: Request): string | null
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How to handle conflicting matches and policy precedence?
- How would you hot-swap policies in a live gateway without dropping requests?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Beginner-friendly exploration of extensibility and non-blocking I/O: add new sinks without changing core, and isolate failures per sink.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy/Plug-in pattern for runtime extension
- Registry mapping names to Sink implementations
- Non-blocking writes via per-sink queuing and worker pool
- Fault isolation and graceful degradation

## Code Example
```typescript
interface Sink { write(msg: string): Promise<void> }
class Registry { addSink(name: string, s: Sink): void; getSinks(): Sink[] }
class Logger { constructor(private reg: Registry) ; log(msg: string): void { for (const s of reg.getSinks()) s.write(msg); } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test sink isolation and backpressure?
- How would you implement graceful shutdown for all sinks?

## Why This Is Asked

Practical multi-tenant routing with runtime extensibility; assesses patterns and trade-offs.

## Key Concepts

- Strategy: channel dispatch per policy
- Registry: per-tenant policy storage
- Composite: policy groups with priorities
- Backpressure: async dispatch and rate limits

## Code Example

```javascript
// Interfaces sketch (simplified)
interface Channel { send(payload: any): Promise<void> }
interface Policy { evaluate(event: any): boolean; channels: string[]; priority: number }
interface PolicyRegistry { register(tenant: string, p: Policy): void; resolve(tenant: string, event: any): Policy[] }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you ensure isolation across tenants during policy updates?
- How would you test performance under burst traffic?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to design runtime-extensible patterns, understand concurrency primitives, and execute safe zero-downtime swaps in production systems.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for pluggable eviction algorithms
- Registry pattern for runtime extensibility without restarts
- AtomicReference for thread-safe strategy swaps
- Per-shard isolation to prevent global bottlenecks and enable granular metrics

## Core Interface
```java
public interface EvictionStrategy<K,V> {
  void onPut(K key, V value);
  void onAccess(K key);
  K evictCandidate();
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle state migration when swapping eviction strategies at runtime?
- What are the performance implications of different eviction strategies?
- How would you implement custom eviction policies that require external coordination?
